URL: https://whatfix.com/ai/screensense/

- "Introducing ScreenSense"

- "Real-time, intuitive assistance that adapts to their needs" / "Contextual, personalized guidance that simplifies complex tasks" / "support users in the flow of work"

**"Userization" is their signature strategic word.** CEO Khadim Batti: "Whatfix AI Agents flip that equation. They **userize** technology to adapt to the user's context." "At the heart of the userization approach is ScreenSense."

---

## Whatfix AI Agents (launched Sept 2025)
URL: https://whatfix.com/newsroom/press-releases/whatfix-launches-ai-agents-to-accelerate-business-outcomes-for-enterprises/

A "unified suite of AI Agents … a native intelligence layer embedded across the Whatfix suite," all powered by ScreenSense, which "continuously interprets both the users' context within an application and the user's real-time intent."

- **Guidance Agent** — "delivers precise, AI-generated answers **in the flow of work**, distilling complex or lengthy knowledge into short, contextual summaries" — so users get clarity "without switching tabs, reading long documents, or escalating."
- **Authoring Agent** — generates "fully configured in-app experiences using simple natural language."
- **Insights Agent** — "ask questions in natural language to uncover user behavior and drop-off patterns."

Executive framing:
- Batti: "This is not just about improving adoption. It is about enabling **every user** to succeed."
- Customer (Servier, Operational Excellence Director): "With Whatfix AI, we're heading towards a world where digital solutions will self-correct, self-improve, and **personalize in real time**."

---

## The STORY FRAME — how they narrate walking an employee through change
From the change-management page (https://whatfix.com/change-management/), verbatim:
- "Enterprise software change management is the discipline of **preparing users, guiding them through changed workflows, and measuring whether the change improves execution once it goes live.**"
- "Strong teams use it to **prepare users before launch, support them in the flow of work after go-live, and improve the workflow as real behavior reveals friction points.**"

The AI-adoption arc is narrated as an awareness-to-value lifecycle: "Empower end-users across the technology adoption lifecycle, from awareness to value" → "drive awareness of new AI capabilities" → "Surface contextual use cases at key moments, nudge users to experiment" → "Support users when they experience frustration" → "Guide users in the flow of work and provide AI assistance" → "Train users with hands-on simulations and AI roleplay in a risk-free sandbox."

Note the frame is **system-centric, not person-centric**: the software adapts to the user ("userize"), rather than a persistent companion accompanying a named individual.

- **Fear of wasted investment / ROI anxiety:** "Deploying AI ≠ Using AI"; "efficiency gains remain theoretical" without adoption. A commissioned study headline: enterprises "Stand to Lose $10.9M Annually Due to Poor Digital Adoption."
- **Relief from complexity:** "so your users don't need to understand your software" — remove the burden of learning from the human.
- **Inevitability / future-facing:** "self-correct, self-improve, and personalize in real time."

---

## Who the buyer is
Whatfix targets **operational/IT/enablement owners, not primarily the CHRO or a "Head of Change" title.** Verbatim role-targeting language:
- "Enterprise Application Owner," "Transformation Program Lead," "IT leaders and application owners," "Business process owners," "Regional leaders," plus "L&D" and "Service desk teams."
- "For **IT leaders and application owners**, its value is practical: reduce disruption, protect process quality, contain support demand, and shorten the time it takes users to become competent on new or updated systems."
- Solution pages also address L&D, HR, Product Teams, and digital-transformation leaders (implied CIO/CHRO/Head of Enablement), but the *named* personas skew toward **app owners, transformation leads, and IT** — the people accountable for a rollout — not an HR change persona.

## CRITICAL question: a personal 1:1 AI companion walking each individual through a change?

**No — Whatfix does not frame a personal 1:1 AI companion.** This is the key differentiator for your positioning:

- Their agents are an **"embedded intelligence layer"** and **"AI Agents"** scoped to functions (Guidance, Authoring, Insights) — tools that serve *whoever* is on a screen, not a persistent companion assigned to a named employee.
- The framing is **software-adapts-to-user ("userize")**, in-the-moment and stateless: "recognizing what users are doing … responding in the moment," "adapts to their needs." It's contextual assistance triggered by screen + intent, not an ongoing relationship.
- The AI-in-DAP blog explicitly frames the agents as **execution-acceleration/information-delivery tools where "humans retain accountability"** — "There is no explicit mention of personalized individual companions or agentic systems operating independently for single employees during change adoption."
- Closest they get: the Guidance Agent surfaces "the right information at the exact moment of need by reading underlying application workflows and user intent" — but that's contextual info delivery inside a workflow, **not a 1:1 companion that accompanies a person through their whole adoption journey.**

The words "personalized," "real-time intent," and "in the flow of work" are everywhere, but "personalized" means *the response is tailored to the current screen/context*, not *a dedicated agent that is yours over time*. There is no "your AI companion," no per-employee persistent agent, no 1:1 relationship framing. That white space is theirs to lose and yours to claim.
